loricatus.definition: lōrīcātus adj. lorica, clothed in mail, harnessed : statua, L.: equites, L.

lotus1.definition: lōtus and lōtos ī, f , lwto/s, the African lotus, edible nettle-tree, V., O.—The fruit of the lotus, O.—A flute (of lotus-wood), O.

lubens.definition: lubēns, lubenter, lubet, lubīdō see lib-.

luce.definition: lūce adv., by daylight, see lux.

luci.definition: lūcī adv., by daylight, see lux.

lucide.definition: lūcidē adv. lucidus, clearly, distinctly : verbum definire.

luctans.definition: luctāns antis, adj. P. of luctor, struggling, reluctant : luctantia oscula carpere, O.

lucto.definition: luctō —, —, āre lucta, a wrestling, to wrestle, struggle : dum luctat, T.

luctuose.definition: lūctuōsē adv. with comp. luctuosus, lamentably, mournfully : luctuosius nobis quam vobis perierunt, L.

luculente.definition: lūculentē adv. luculentus, splsndidly, well : scripserunt: alqm calefacere, i. e. flog well .

luculenter.definition: lūculenter adv. luculentus, very well : sane luculenter, very well said : Graece scire.

lucus1.definition: lūcus ī, m LVC-, a sacred grove, consecrated wood, park surrounding a temple : Albani luci: frequenti silvā saeptus, L.: virtutem verba putas et Lucum ligna, H.: laetissimus umbrae, V.— A wood, grove , V., O.

lucus2.definition: (lūcus, ūs) m light (old for lux): cum primo lucu, at daybreak, T. (al. luci).

lucusta.definition: lucusta (loc-) ae, f 4 LAC-, a grasshopper, locust : lucustarum nubes, L.: vis locustarum, Ta.

ludicer.definition: (lūdicer) cra, crum, adj. ludus, belonging to play, serving for sport, done in sport, sportive : exercitatio: Praemia, awarded in the games , V.: res, the drama , H.

ludificor.definition: lūdificor ātus, ārī, dep. ludus+2 FAC-, to mock, make game of, make sport of, turn into ridicule, delude, deceive : aperte: me, T.: inter se, L. — To thwart, frustrate, baffle : morā consulem, S.: ea, quae hostes ager…

lugubre.definition: lūgubre adv. lugubris, mournfully, portentously : cometae rubent, V.

lunatus.definition: lūnātus adj. P. of luno, half-moon-shaped, crescent-shaped, lunated, falcated : peltae, V.

lupatus.definition: lupātus adj. lupus, furnished with wolf teeth : Gallia nec lupatis Temperat ora frenis, curbs studded with jagged points , H.—Plur n . as subst, a curb armed with sharp teeth : duris parere lupatis, V., O.

lustrum1.definition: lustrum ī, n 3 LV-, a slough, bog, haunt, den of beasts : ferarum Lustra, V.— A wood, forest, wilderness : horrentia lustra, V.: per devia lustra, O.— A house of ill-repute : tenebrae lustrorum.— Fig., debauchery : vi…

lustrum2.definition: lūstrum ī, n 3 LV-, a purificatory sacrifice, expiatory offering, lustration (for the whole people by the censors at the end of their term of five years): lustrum condidit, made the lustral sacrifice : sub lustrum cen…

lusus2.definition: lūsus ūs, m ludo, a playing, play, game : per lusum, for sport , L.: fugio lusum trigonem (i. e. trigonalem), H.: virgineis exercent lusibus undas Naides, O.— Dalliance , O., Pr.

luteus1.definition: lūteus adj. 1 lutum, colored with yellowweed, golden-yellow, saffron-yellow, orange-yellow : pallor, H.: sulphura, O.: palla, Tb.— Rose-colored, rosy, rose-red : Aurora, V., O.: soccus, Ct.

luteus2.definition: luteus adj. 2 lutum, of mud, of clay : Rheni caput, H.: opus, of a swallow's nest , O.— Besmeared, bedaubed : Volcanus, Iu.— Fig., dirty, vile, worthless : homo: negotium, a poor affair .

lutum1.definition: lūtum ī, n a plant yielding a yellow dye, yellow-weed, dyer's weed, weld: croceum, V.: luto corpora tingere, i. e. with yellow, Tb.

lutum2.definition: lutum ī, n 3 LV-, mud, mire : volutari in luto: crates luto integuntur, Cs.: imbre lutoque Adspersus, H.: Pinguia crura luto, Iu.: te pervolvam in luto, T.—Prov.: in eodem luto haesitas, you are in the same difficulty…

luxurior.definition: lūxurior ātus, ārī, dep., to wanton, revel: meo malo. O.

luxuriose.definition: lūxuriōsē adv. with comp. luxuriosus, luxuriously, voluptuously : vivere: exercitum habere, S.: luxuriosius epulari, N.

lymphatus.definition: lymphātus lympha, distracted, frantic, beside oneself : exercitum pavor invasit: lymphati et attoniti, L.: furit lymphata per urbem, V.: pectora, O.: mens, H.

lynx.definition: lynx lyncis, m and f , lu/gc, a lynx: lynces Bacchi variae (Bacchus was drawn by a team of lynxes), V.: Colla lyncum, O.: timidos lyncas, H.
